note: 2026-09-24 전수 감사 — 9개 차원 + 비평가의 공백 4개. 각 발견은 독립 검증자가 재현을 시도했다. 빌드 efe8710 을 고정해 대고 잤다.
critic:
이번 감사는 형식은 전수에 가깝게 봤지만, 사실 검증과 실행 환경은 얇은 표본에 머물렀다. 링크, 레이아웃, 데이터 정합성, 문, 판본 행 형식은 기계로 전수 점검했고 수준이 높다. 6,097쪽 크롤, 2개 폭 레이아웃, 7,678개 문 질의, 1,796개 판본 행 체크섬이 여기 든다. 반면 네 곳이 비어 있다.

(1) 사실 검증이 36명 wave 코호트에 몰렸다. 붉은 인장을 달고 검색에 색인되는 검토 도판 38개는 이번 감사에서 한 문장도 독립 대조되지 않았다(facts 표본 10개와 기계 스윕 36개 모두 wave 작가다. 교집합 0). 매주 첫 장에 걸리는 174명 가운데 138명도 대조하지 않았다. 스케치는 1,642개 중 30개만 봤는데, 그 30개에서 4개가 틀렸다. 이 비율이면 약 200개 스케치가 틀렸다고 추정되지만 위치는 모른다. 작품 의의 문단은 964개 중 약 10개, 관계 요약은 487개 중 약 130개만 봤다.

(2) 실행 환경은 전부 Chrome/Blink였다. WebKit·iOS Safari, 실제 폰, 한글 IME 조합 입력은 한 번도 돌리지 않았다.

(3) 제품 약속의 뒷절 「일주일 뒤 스스로 돌아온다」가 기대는 저장소 생존을 아무도 재지 않았다. 사파리 7일 삭제, 카카오톡 등 인앱 브라우저의 별도 저장소, 그리고 백업이라던 로그인이 일반 독자에게는 막혀 있을 가능성(추정)이 모두 걸려 있는데, 이 셋을 이은 감사자가 없다. docs/backend-design.md:173의 「실제 아이폰으로 7일 실측」은 2026-09-03부터 ⏳ 상태 그대로다.

(4) 도판 79건의 출처·라이선스 기록은 아무도 원 파일 페이지와 대조하지 않았다.

그래서 「전체 점검 제대로 했나」에 대한 정직한 답은 이렇다. 기계가 전수할 수 있는 구조 결함은 거의 다 잡았다. 그러나 사이트가 가장 크게 내건 약속 셋은 검증되지 않았다. 붉은 인장의 사실성, 매주 보여 주는 작가의 사실성, 일주일 뒤 서재가 남아 있는가. 아래 다섯 공백 가운데 앞의 셋이 닫히기 전에는 이번 감사를 '전체 점검'이라고 부를 수 없다.

findings.title: The name search strips the letter 's' and all digits but keeps spaces, so 60% of Korean names typed without a space fail (lost backslashes in lpNorm)
findings.where: dist/index.html inline script `function lpNorm` (source scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:1090, inside a TS template literal)
findings.impact: This is the first thing the product offers: 「아는 이름에서 펴기」. A reader who types a famous author's name without a space is told the book does not have them, even when the author is a reviewed plate. Or they are handed four unrelated names. The existing contract passes only because its test name, 도스토예프스키, is a space-free alias.
findings.fix: Escape the backslashes in the template literal (`\\s`, `\\-`) or write the regex with String.raw. Add a contract for 조지오웰 and 1984.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. The shipped lpNorm is `/[s·.,-_'’]/g` (dist/index.html). The source at scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:1090 is `/[\s·.,\-_'’]/g`, inside a template literal that ate the backslashes. Replaying the shipped matcher over all 1,540 spaced Korean names typed without the space: 618 open the right author, 523 get 「찾지 못했다」, 94 open the wrong author and 305 get a list. The target is absent from 28 of those lists, not 40 as claimed. 51 of the misses are plates. The intended regex resolves 1540/1540. In the browser at 375 px: 조지오웰 and 토니모리슨 give 「이 이름으로는 찾지 못했다」, 1984 gives 「여럿이 걸린다 — 라빈드라나트 타고르 · 나쓰메 소세키 · 루쉰 · 아쿠타가와 류노스케」, and Hesse gives 「은희경 · 헤르만 헤세」. The door contract at qa/verify-book.mjs:606 passes only because its test name, 도스토예프스키, has no space and no 's'.

findings.title: The door opens a different person without saying so (3-character prefix fuzz plus plate preference)
findings.where: dist/index.html door submit handler: `n.length>=4&&x.indexOf(n.slice(0,3))===0&&Math.abs(x.length-n.length)<=2` and `if(pl.length)part=pl; if(part.length===1)hit=...`
findings.impact: A reader asks for one person and is shown another as if it were the answer. There is no 「가까운 이름」 hint. This is the product 'saying something untrue' at the moment it is trying to win the reader's trust, and it can lead to marking a book by the wrong author.
findings.fix: Open silently only on an exact key match. For fuzzy hits, show 「이 이름은 없다 — 혹시: …」 and let the reader choose.

verdict.reason: Reproduced in the browser. 무라카미 류 opens #haruki-murakami. 알랭 드 보통 opens 알랭 로브그리예 and 안나 카레니나 opens 안나 아흐마토바. Neither case shows a notice: the page text contains nothing about 류 or any 「가까운 이름」 hint. Part of this is independent of the regex bug. With the intended regex, 무라카미 류 still opens 하루키, 알랭 드 보통 opens 알랭 드 릴, Saint Exupery opens 야레드, 게이 opens 히가시노 게이고 and 제임스 opens 헨리 제임스, because of the 3-character prefix fuzz and plate preference. The title cases (안나 카레니나, 해리 포터) come from the kept space and would become plain misses once the regex is fixed. I downgraded the severity to medium because the opened author's real name is printed as the h2, so the reader can notice the switch.

findings.title: The door does not search book titles, which the index does. Title typers hit a dead end or a wrong person, and some queries fail in both places
findings.where: dist/index.html door (keys are name/orig/aliases only) vs dist/authors/index.html (data-h includes titles)
findings.impact: Readers who 'can't choose' often remember a book, not a name. The contract's 15-minute path gains a detour or ends outright.
findings.fix: Fall back to titles in the door using the same data the index has. Normalize spaces in the index too. Add 상실의 시대 as an alternate title.

verdict.reason: The door does miss titles: 데미안 gives 「이 이름으로는 찾지 못했다 — 색인에서 「데미안」 찾기」. But the miss message links straight to the index, and the index resolves 데미안, 채식주의자, 82년생 김지영 and 안나 카레니나 (one match each). So title typers get a working detour, not a dead end. The door is also labelled as a name door (placeholder 「좋아한 작가 이름」). The strings that fail in both places are real: 조지오웰, 세익스피어, 애거서 크리스티 and 상실의 시대 all get 「…에 맞는 이름이 없다」 in the index. Those failures come from index spacing, missing aliases, and 상실의 시대 not being an alternate title. They are not caused by the door lacking titles. The wrong-person outcome for title queries duplicates the silent-wrong-author finding.

findings.title: The front-page walk labels plain chronological lists 「여기서 읽기 시작한다면」 for 1,630 sketch and silhouette authors whose own pages say no entry order exists
findings.where:
dist/index.html render(): `if(a.works.length){ html+='

여기서 읽기 시작한다면

'+lpWorks(a,true); }` (applied regardless of depth)
findings.impact: The walk presents a year-sorted list as curated reading advice. That contradicts the author's own page and the motto 「지어내지 않는다」, and it steers the reader to the oldest book (낙원의 이쪽 rather than 위대한 개츠비).
findings.fix: Use the 「여기서 읽기 시작한다면」 heading only for plates that have an entry order; use 「책 N」 otherwise.

verdict.reason:
render() in dist/index.html emits `

여기서 읽기 시작한다면

` whenever a.works.length is non-zero, whatever the depth. All 1,630 non-plate capsules that have works list them in year order. The door view for F. 스콧 피츠제럴드 reads 「아직 실루엣이다 — … / 여기서 읽기 시작한다면 / 낙원의 이쪽 1920 / 위대한 개츠비 1925 …」. The static sketch page for stephen-king says 「입문 순서와 판본은 아직 우리가 놓지 않았다」 and heads the same list 「책 3」. The front page therefore presents a year-sorted list as reading advice.

findings.title: Walking author to author on the front page leaves no history. Phone Back skips every step and leaves the book
findings.where: dist/index.html `function go(id){...history.replaceState(null,'','#'+id);render(id);}`
findings.impact: On a phone, Back is the main navigation. A reader exploring 「다음 걸음」 who presses Back to return to the previous author is thrown out: to the previous page, or out of the site entirely if they came from a search or messenger link. They lose their place.
findings.fix: Use pushState for hops and render on popstate, or make the trail crumbs links.

verdict.reason:
go() uses history.replaceState, and dist/index.html contains no pushState and no popstate handler. Repro: /shelf/ → / → door 카프카 → two 다음 걸음 hops. history.length stays 3 throughout, and goBack() lands on /shelf/. The trail 「프란츠 카프카 → 호르헤 루이스 보르헤스 → 미겔 데 세르반테스」 is a plain

, not links.

findings.title: A returning reader's weekly page is driven by one mark for 12 weeks. Other marks never surface, and nothing acknowledges the return
findings.where: dist/atlas.js openAt()/readiness(): pool = ready.slice(0,12), scored by level (read=3 dominates)
findings.impact: The contract's second half, coming back on their own a week later, depends on each week's page feeling personal. One high mark crowds out the rest, so a reader whose tastes span several authors sees the same reason every week.
findings.fix: Rotate the 'from' author across weeks, for example by capping the share of the pool one source may take.

verdict.reason: Reproduced with the clock advanced weekly over 12 weeks and four seeded marks (Kafka read, Camus want, Han Kang opened, Murakami have). Every one of the 12 weekly pages is sourced from Kafka: 9 × 「프란츠 카프카를 읽었으니 이제 열린다」 and 3 × 「…와 같은 때, 같은 자리에 있었다」. The Han Kang, Murakami and Camus marks never produce a page. Two parts of the claim are overstated. First, a different author opens each week (샐린저, 마르케스, 쿤데라 …), so the pages themselves are not repeated. Second, the page does acknowledge the reader: it leads with a reason drawn from their own reading and shows 「만난 작가 4 / 1837」. What is real is narrower: one high mark crowds out the others as the source of the weekly page.

findings.title: 「도감 지키기」 is offered on every page, but without SMTP the default Supabase mailer refuses non-team addresses. Inferred, not exercised live
findings.where: #lp-auth box on all pages (book.js paintAuth); docs/backend-design.md:22 「SMTP 미설정(Supabase 기본 메일러)」; STATUS.md:41; book.js sendErrorKo comment 「기본 메일러는 프로젝트 팀 주소에만 보낸다」
findings.impact: Any reader outside the team who trusts the offer to keep their shelf across devices hits a refusal after typing their email. The page states it honestly, but it is an unfinished feature presented on every page.
findings.fix: Configure SMTP, or hide the box until it can deliver.

verdict.reason: Not observable without sending a real magic link, which is forbidden. The mechanism rests on the project's own code and docs. book.js has the comment 「기본 메일러는 프로젝트 팀 주소에만 보낸다」 and sendErrorKo maps the refusal to 「이 주소로는 아직 메일을 보낼 수 없다」. docs/backend-design.md:22 says 「SMTP 미설정(Supabase 기본 메일러)」, and :153 notes a limit of about 3–4 mails per hour. STATUS.md:41 hedges: 「보내지 않을 수 있다」. The failure is stated honestly, and marks stay on the device, so the core contract (mark locally, return) is unaffected. It is an unfinished, secondary feature, so I rated it low.

findings.title: On a cold cache, the returning reader waits 3.5–4× longer than a new visitor for the front page, and every author page downloads the graph even with no marks
findings.where: dist/index.html openBook() (marks → A.graph() before render); book.js paintReadiness() always imports atlas and fetches /graph.json
findings.impact: The reader the contract most wants back gets the slowest first screen. Phones often evict the cache within a week.
findings.fix: Precompute or split the readiness data a returning reader needs. Skip graph.json in paintReadiness when the reader has no marks.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is confirmed. openBook waits for A.graph() (graph.json, 658,925 B raw) before rendering when marks exist. paintReadiness always calls A.graph() before checking lit, so an author page fetches graph.json for a reader with zero marks. The size of the gap is not reproduced. My frozen throttled run (1.6 Mbps, 150 ms, CPU×4, to #app h2 after load) measured 5.7 s fresh and 9.2 s returning, about 1.6×, not 3.5–4×. I did not re-measure live.

findings.title: In production, missing pages return 200 with the front page. A dead link is never told 「없다」
findings.where: Cloudflare Pages deployment (no 404.html in dist)
findings.impact: A mistyped or outdated shared link lands on 「이번 주에 열린 쪽」 with no sign the page is gone, which runs against 「없는 것은 없다고 적는다」. It also creates soft-404s for search engines.
findings.fix: Ship a 404.html that says the page does not exist and links to the index.

verdict.reason: Reproduced on live. /authors/nobody/ returns 200 text/html with a body byte-identical to dist/index.html, and /walk/nobody.json also returns 200 text/html. dist has no 404.html. This is a known platform behaviour, noted at qa/verify-book.mjs:286, but it is still unfixed, and dead shared links silently land on the weekly page.

findings.title: The literacy map says where you can 'read without a map', yet a single 관심 있는 책 fills it
findings.where: dist/index.html literacyBlock + atlas.js literacy() (lit includes want=1)
findings.impact: This is a mild overclaim about the reader, on a surface that sells itself as honest.
findings.fix: Count only opened, have and read marks, or change the sentence.

verdict.reason: atlas.js litAuthors weights want at 1, and literacyBlock passes that lit set straight to literacy(), which counts met = lit.has(a.i). With a single 「관심 있는 책」 mark (노르웨이의 숲), the map reads 「배지가 아니다. 어디를 지도 없이 읽을 수 있는지를 말한다. … 동아시아 1/144」. Meanwhile KIND_KO deliberately avoids 「읽었으니」 for want marks. The claim holds as stated, and it is a mild overclaim.

findings.title: The drop cap splits years: 「1 980년 5월」 on 163 work pages and 17 author pages
findings.where: book.css:100 `.lede.cap::first-letter` applied to ledes that start with a digit
findings.impact: The year becomes hard to read on the first line of the page.
findings.fix: Skip the drop cap when the first character is a digit, or cap the whole number.

verdict.reason: book.css:100 `.lede.cap::first-letter{float:left;font-size:3.5em…}` applies to ledes that start with a digit. A grep counts 163 work pages and 17 author pages. The screenshot shows a large 「1」 followed by 「980년 5월 광주…」.

findings.title: Every novel is labelled 「소설·단편」 on 2,089 work pages
findings.where: src/types.ts:509 `{ id: "fiction", ko: "소설·단편" }`, rendered in the work-page label line
findings.impact: A Korean reader can take 「소설·단편」 on a long novel to mean it is a short story.
findings.fix: Use 「소설」, or split novel and short story.

verdict.reason: 「소설·단편」 is rendered on 2,089 work pages (for example 노르웨이의 숲 「· 1987 · 소설·단편」 and 채식주의자), from src/types.ts:509. It is a category label: the middle dot means 'novels and short stories', not a claim that the work is a short story. The ambiguity for a Korean reader is real but mild. The auditor's tally line 「단편 2089」 misstates the label text.

findings.title: After the door or a hop, the page scrolls to its own top. The chosen author sits at the fold and their books are below it
findings.where: dist/index.html render(): `window.scrollTo(0,0)`
findings.impact: Every hop sends the reader back to the title and door, and they must scroll about 1.5 screens to reach the books they asked for.
findings.fix: Scroll #app into view instead of the window top.

verdict.reason: render() calls window.scrollTo(0,0). After the door or a hop, scrollY is 0 and the chosen author's h2 sits at about 685–703 px of an 812 px viewport, so only the name shows above the fold.

findings.title: Common Korean spellings and bestseller authors are missing, while the lede claims 「세계는 처음부터 전부 여기 있고」
findings.where: dist/walk-22f1ebf923.json aliases; front-page lede
findings.impact: Korean readers' most likely inputs fail. The miss message is honest, but the lede's scope claim is not, and the docs treat scope as a data claim.
findings.fix: Add variant aliases and soften the lede to state the real scope.

findings.title: Every relation row on the site shows '·' instead of →, ← or ↔, so the reader can't tell who influenced whom
findings.where: scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:89 (GLYPH map), used at :349 (relRow), :618 (work-page relList) and :900 (front-page capsule hops); src/book/relations.ts relationGlyph()
findings.impact: Direction is the main claim of an influence edge, and the reader now gets '· 영향' from both sides. Nothing tells them the edge's source is its origin, so an honest directed claim reads as a symmetric tag. Only the prose summary, when it happens to say, recovers the direction. This affects every author page with relations, work pages that show connected people, and the '다음 걸음' step on the front page.
findings.fix: Map the glyph characters directly: const g = relationGlyph(r, selfId) at all three call sites. Or re-key GLYPH by '→', '←', '↔'. Then add a contract that some directed relation renders → on the source page and ← on the target page.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly. GLYPH at scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:89 is keyed {out,in,both}, but relationGlyph() in src/book/relations.ts:47 returns '→'/'←'/'↔'. So GLYPH[...] is always undefined and every row falls back to '·'. This happens at all three call sites (:349 relRow, :618 work relList, :900 capsule hops). I could not find any verify-book contract or unit test that checks the rendered glyph. Nothing on the page is false: the summary sentence usually states the direction. But the glyph was built to carry the direction claim, and it is missing on every relation row across the site, with directed and bidirectional relations now rendered the same.

findings.title: Edition tables at 720px and wider break years, translator names and publisher names mid-word: a year prints as '201' on one line and '4' on the next
findings.where: All work pages with edition tables in table layout (viewport ≥720px), including desktop. book.css: .eds .yr has no white-space:nowrap and inherits body{overflow-wrap:anywhere}. Meanwhile .eds .isbn and .eds .get are nowrap, so in auto table layout they take the width and squeeze the text columns.
findings.impact: On a page whose job is to present verified editions, a reader sees '201' or '199' as the edition year. On a verified record, that reads as wrong or corrupted data, which undercuts the 'we don't make things up' promise. It happens on ordinary desktop widths and on tablets or phones in landscape (720–915px).
findings.fix: Put white-space:nowrap on .eds .yr and word-break:keep-all with overflow-wrap:normal (or break-word) on .eds .tr and .eds .pub. Give .eds .pub a min-width such as 8em, or wrap the three links in .get so they don't monopolise the width. Add a contract that no .yr cell has more than one line box at 768, 900 and 1280.

verdict.reason: I reproduced this exactly, and the counts match. .eds .yr has no nowrap and inherits body{overflow-wrap:anywhere} (book.css:27, 264), while .isbn and .get are nowrap (265–266). It still looks like broken data in the table that is meant to present verified editions.

Add a contract that ISBN and .oop boxes never intersect link boxes at 320, 360 and 375 on every edition page. The existing contract only tests document overflow on 5 pages, which passes here: nothing overflows the page, the text just collides.

findings.title: 『노르웨이의 숲』 페이지: 한국어판이 1989년 『상실의 시대』로 '처음' 나왔다고 틀리게 적음
findings.where: /works/haruki-murakami--noruwei-no-mori/ (data/works/plate-wave-kr.json의 haruki-murakami--noruwei-no-mori significance; 근거는 qc/wave-kr-2026-09/gen/haruki-murakami.json)
findings.impact: 도판 페이지에서 '처음'이라는 확인 불가능한 최상급 사실을 틀리게 단정했다. 실제로는 1988년 원제 그대로 여러 판이 먼저 나왔다. 독자가 스스로 확인할 수 없는 부분이 모토 「지어내지 않는다」와 어긋난다. 또 생성기가 출판사 소개문을 사실로 옮겨 적는 경로가 실제로 틀린 결과를 낸다는 증거다. 36개 도판의 근거는 대부분 출판사·서점 소개문이다.
findings.fix: 「한국에서는 1988년 『노르웨이의 숲』으로 처음 번역됐고, 1989년 문학사상사가 『상실의 시대』로 정식 계약해 내며 널리 읽혔다」처럼 고치거나, '처음'을 빼고 1989년 문학사상사판만 적는다.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. The frozen build's /works/haruki-murakami--noruwei-no-mori/ says 「한국에서는 1989년 『상실의 시대』라는 제목으로 처음 나왔다.」 That is wrong: Korean editions under the original title came out in 1988, and 문학사상사's 『상실의 시대』 followed in 1989. The error sits on a plate page, where a reader expects the text to be sourced, and the only source behind it is a publisher's blurb. The sentence also uses 「처음」, which docs/editorial-guide.md:45 forbids in importanceReason (this text is a work significance, but the same principle applies). Medium stands: the fact is small, but the pipeline repeating publisher copy is exactly how the project's honesty breaks.

findings.title: 관계 유형 과장: 근거가 '영향'·'대화'를 뒷받침하지 않는데 그 딱지를 붙인 관계 3개
findings.where: data/relations/plate-wave-kr.json: influence--baek-seok--kim-yeon-su (/authors/kim-yeon-su/, '백석 · 영향'), dialogue--jeong-ji-yong--yi-hyo-seok (/authors/yi-hyo-seok/, '정지용 · 대화'), influence--park-wan-suh--kim-ae-ran (/authors/kim-ae-ran/)
findings.impact: 요약문은 정직한데 페이지의 관계 딱지(· 영향 / · 대화)와 선의 굵기(weight 0.7–0.8)가 요약보다 강하게 주장한다. 딱지만 보는 독자는 '백석이 김연수에게 영향을 줬다'는 추론을 사실로 받아들이게 된다.
findings.fix: (a)는 관계를 빼거나 affinity(scholarly_consensus 출처가 있을 때)로 낮춘다. (b)는 dialogue를 빼거나 affinity로 낮춘다. (c)는 dialogue로 바꾼다.

verdict.reason: All three reproduced. docs/relations-guide.md:26/29 defines documented_influence as 「확인된 직접 영향」 and dialogue as 「실질 교류·우정·공개 논쟁」. (a) influence--baek-seok--kim-yeon-su is documented_influence at weight 0.8, but its summary only says that 김연수 wrote a novel modelled on 백석. That makes 백석 a subject, not an influence. (b) dialogue--jeong-ji-yong--yi-hyo-seok is dialogue at 0.7, and its own summary admits 「그 이상의 교류 기록은 찾지 못했다」, so it fails the definition by its own words. (c) influence--park-wan-suh--kim-ae-ran is documented_influence at 0.7, backed by a prize judging, a mourning remark and an anthology recommendation. That is evidence of contact, not of influence on her writing. The summaries are honest, but the page labels 「· 영향」 and 「· 대화」 claim more than they do. Low severity is right.

findings.title: 스케치 김정희: 『완당전집(阮堂全集)』을 '1867 초간'으로 적음. 실제로는 1934년 간행
findings.where: /authors/kim-jeong-hui/ (data/works/silhouette-wave1.json의 kim-jeong-hui--wandang-jeonjip, year 1867, yearBasis first-print)
findings.impact: 책 이름과 초간 연도가 서로 다른 책의 것이다. 초간이 67년 앞당겨져 있다. 스케치 페이지가 '연도는 아직 출처에 대보지 않았다'고 밝히고 있어서 심각도는 낮다.
findings.fix: year를 1934로 고친다. 또는 1867년 문집을 원하면 『완당척독』이나 『담연재시고』로 바꾼다.

verdict.reason: The defect is real but not quite as stated. The page shows 「완당전집 / 1867 초간」, and 1867 is wrong for any version of this collection: that year saw only 《담연재시고》 and 《완당척독》. However, the same ITKC 일러두기 the auditor relied on treats the 1934 신조선사 《완당(선생)전집》 as a 重刊本 of a collection first printed (初刊) in 1868 by 남병길 and 민규호 as 《완당집》. So the finding's 'actually 1934, 67 years early' is only one reading. By ITKC's own account the first print of the collection is 1868; 1934 is the year of the edition carrying the 전집 title. Either the year becomes 1934 with the 전집 title, or it becomes 1868 with the title changed to 완당집. The sketch page states that it has not been checked against sources yet.

findings.title: 생존 작가 규칙('사생활·논란은 쓰지 않는다') 위반: 수감, 정신병원 경험, 사적인 추모 트윗
findings.where: /authors/hwang-sok-yong/ importanceReason; /works/paulo-coelho--veronika-decide-morrer/ significance; /authors/eun-hee-kyung/ 관계 dialogue--park-wan-suh--eun-hee-kyung
findings.impact: 셋 다 출처가 있고 사실이다. 하지만 생존 인물의 법적 이력(맥락이 빠져 있어 범죄 이력처럼 읽힐 수 있음), 젊은 시절 정신병원 경험(건강), 사적인 감정을 페이지에 단정적으로 적었다. 프로젝트가 스스로 정한 보수적 서술 규칙과 어긋난다.
findings.fix: (a) 「1993년 방북으로 수감됐다가 1998년 풀려난 뒤」처럼 공적 맥락을 넣거나 「1998년 이후」로만 쓴다. (b) 문장을 빼거나 「작가는 이 소설이 자기 젊은 날의 경험에 부분적으로 기댔다고 말했다」처럼 본인 발언으로 돌린다. (c) 출판기념회 회고만 남기고 트윗 속 후회 내용은 뺀다.

verdict.reason: All three texts render as quoted, but the finding frames them wrongly. (a) 황석영: this is the one real defect, and it is a missing-context problem, not a private-life breach. His 1993–98 imprisonment for the 1989 방북 is public political history. But no other line on the page mentions imprisonment or 방북, so 「1998년 석방 뒤로는」 comes out of nowhere and reads like an unexplained criminal record. (b) 코엘료: Coelho has spoken publicly about his psychiatric institutionalisation, and the novel is openly based on it. Stating it on the work page is attributed public biography tied to the work, so it is borderline at most. (c) 은희경: the tweets were public and reported by 한국일보. Paraphrasing her published regret is mild and sourced, though it is the most personal detail of the three. I would fix (a) and optionally soften (c); (b) is not a violation.

findings.title: 스케치 문장 2개가 출처로 확인되지 않는 '처음·들여왔다' 주장을 함
findings.where: /authors/muriel-spark/, /authors/walther-von-der-vogelweide/ (importanceReason, depth sketch)
findings.impact: 페이지가 '아직 출처에 대보지 않았다'고 밝히고 있어서 영향은 작다. 다만 스케치 30개 중 2개(6.7%)가 최초성을 과장한다는 표본 신호다. 편집 지침은 「최초·유일·모든·가장」을 출처가 정확히 그만큼 말할 때만 허용한다.
findings.fix: 「…를 쓰는 방법을 영국 소설에서 가장 날카롭게 밀고 나갔다」처럼 좁히거나, 최초성 주장을 빼고 무엇을 했는지만 적는다.

verdict.reason: Both sentences reproduce, but the auditor understated the problem: it is a corpus-wide pattern, not 2 in 30. docs/editorial-guide.md:45 bans outright 「최초·처음·유일·열었다·들여왔다 를 쓰지 않는다」 in importanceReason; it does not merely allow such words when a source supports them, as the finding says. An exhaustive scan of data/authors finds 161 of the 1,642 sketches (about 10%) using at least one banned word: 열었다 55, 들여왔다 45, 처음 41, 최초 18, 유일 9. Both plate hits (han-kang's first Korean Nobel, higashino's 「처음부터」) are true or not superlatives. Machine checks over everything the build draws:
(1) Text extraction. Parsed all 6,097 HTML pages (1,838 author pages including the index, 4,256 work pages, front page, /walk/, shelf) plus 1,837 walk/*.json files and the 487 graph.json edges into 59,412 distinct text blocks (script: prose/blocks.json). Also scanned 24,807 data strings, 3,875 of them prose fields.
(2) Particle agreement after non-Hangul endings. Covers Latin letters, digits (with Korean readings of 십, 백, 천, 만), Han characters and kana, closing brackets, and trailing parentheticals, which were skipped per the Korean convention. Particles: 을/를, 은/는, 이/가, 과/와, 으로/로 (with the ㄹ rule), 이라는/라는, 이나/나, 이며/며, 이다/다, 였다/이었다 and others. 1,955 instances checked; every ambiguous one was reviewed by hand. Result: 1 minor error, 「Felszámolás이」 in an edition note.
(3) Particle agreement after Hangul, for the low-noise classes (를/와 after a final consonant, 으로 after no final consonant or after ㄹ, 과/을 after no final consonant, 로 after a non-ㄹ final consonant, 가, 은, 라는, 라고). Every distinct token was reviewed. 0 errors. Lists: josa_nonhangul.txt, josa_hangul.txt.
(4) The runtime josa() in public/atlas.js. Verified that all 1,837 names.ko values end in a Hangul syllable, so its output is correct.
(5) Budget trimming. firstSentence (the /다\./ cut) run on every importanceReason, readingEntryReason and significance: no fragment cut mid-sentence and no unbalanced brackets (2 false positives were apostrophes). firstSentences(240) on all 487 graph.json edges: 457 are whole summaries and 5 are cut at a sentence boundary. One loses its closing period: dialogue--park-wan-suh--eun-hee-kyung ends '…(한국일보 2011. 1. 23.)' with no final period.
(6) Anaphora scans for text that cannot stand on its own when drawn alone: '같은 X' openings, and '같은 X' with no antecedent in the same text. All hits were reviewed and then placed page by page (antecedent before it or not) and hop by hop in the walk data.
(7) Name consistency. Checked Hangul aliases used in prose instead of names.ko. Ran a jamo edit-distance search (distance 1–2) of every author surname against all prose word types, reviewing 330 candidate pairs by hand. Grepped a curated list of about 150 variant spellings.
(8) Work-title consistency. Every quoted 『』 and 「」 title in text tied to an author was compared with that author's titleKo list (bigram similarity at 0.2 or higher; 93 pairs reviewed).
(9) Transcription rules on all 1,837 names.ko. Checked ㅈ/ㅊ followed by a diphthong, 된소리 (all hits were Vietnamese or Thai, which the rules allow), 쉬, long vowels, word-initial aspirated consonants in the 37 Japanese names (0 violations), and the 1911 cut-off for the 73 Chinese-script authors (0 violations).
(10) Latin and Chinese/Japanese characters outside brackets in all 3,875 prose fields (leak_latin.txt, leak_han.txt), plus Han and kana runs that are not parenthetical glosses (71 runs).
(11) Spacing: double spaces, space before punctuation, missing spaces, space before a particle, doubled words.
(12) Register: every Korean string literal in book.js, atlas.js and the inline page scripts, and a grep of the 14 pages with polite endings (all were real titles or quotations except one UI string).
(13) 번역투 pattern counts (그녀, 에 있어서, 에 의해, 되어지, 로부터의, 을 가진, 중 하나, and others). Counts are low: 그녀 8, 에 의해 5, 에 있어서 1. Not reported as a defect.
(14) Drop-cap first characters on all 1,157 'lede cap' paragraphs.
(15) Back-to-back repetition between the reading-entry reason and the entry work's significance for all 193 plates.

Reading. 62 pages rendered in Playwright (Chrome, 390px, Supabase routes intercepted) and read end to end from innerText: 10 reviewed plates, 8 draft plates, 14 sketches, both silhouettes, 26 work pages (8 with opening sentences, 10 with significance, 8 silhouette works), the index and the shelf. The front page was read fresh, through the door (도스토예프스키, 카프카, 김), on its failure path, and with the literacy map open. The readiness badge was checked in 6 marked-reader scenarios. Screenshots are in /tmp/onebook-audit-0924/prose/shots/ (work-botchan, author-hugo, author-gower-sketch, cap-*.png, front-*.png, ready-kafka-after-flaubert.png).

coverage.counts: Scale checked: 6,097 HTML pages; 59,412 distinct drawn text blocks; 24,807 data strings (3,875 prose fields); 1,955 particle instances after non-Hangul endings; 1,157 drop-cap ledes; 487 graph edges; 1,837 names checked against transcription rules; 62 pages read end to end; 6 readiness-badge scenarios; 17 findings.

findings.title: Ten relation summaries lean on another relation ('같은 …'), but are drawn alone: on author pages, in the front page's 다음 걸음, and as the only line a returning reader gets
findings.where: data/relations/* ids: influence--franz-kafka--yu-hua, influence--gustave-flaubert--franz-kafka, influence--william-faulkner--toni-morrison, influence--kim-seung-ok--hwang-jung-eun, translation--elias-canetti--imre-kertesz, translation--ryunosuke-akutagawa--lu-xun, influence--arthur-conan-doyle--bernard-werber, influence--antoine-de-saint-exupery--bernard-werber, influence--gustave-flaubert--bernard-werber, translation--ernest-hemingway--chairil-anwar. Drawn by public/book.js paintReadiness (row.why), generate-static-pages.ts pageHtml (open.why), walk hops, and the relation lists on author and work pages.
findings.impact: A reader who comes back meets a reference to a letter, interview, thesis or chronicle that was never mentioned. It reads as a fragment or an error, and it lands exactly on the 'one reason' line the generator calls the returning reader's only reward (generate-static-pages.ts, comment above the m field).
findings.fix: Rewrite the ten summaries to name their own document (e.g. '위화는 『파리 리뷰』 인터뷰에서…'). Add a validator rule that rejects a relation summary opening with '같은' plus a noun that has no antecedent in the same summary.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. All 10 summaries are in the data as described. In graph.json the `m` field keeps the dangling '같은 …' opening for 9 of the edges; the Hemingway→Anwar one ends with '같은 번역 목록에 함께 실린 항목이다', which is milder. My own Playwright run (one read mark, then the author page's #lp-ready) shows the badge prints the dangling sentence straight after '…를 읽었으니 이제 열린다.' for Kafka, Yu Hua, Toni Morrison and Bernard Werber. On the static /authors/toni-morrison/ the Faulkner line ('같은 1955년 석사논문…') is drawn before the Woolf line that introduces the thesis. On /authors/antoine-de-saint-exupery/ (reviewStatus=reviewed) the one featured '이어지는 한 사람' line opens with '베르베르는 같은 자전 연보에서'. The walk JSONs for kim-seung-ok, elias-canetti, toni-morrison and ryunosuke-akutagawa carry the same sentences. I downgraded it from high to medium: nothing is invented and the rest of each sentence reads fine, so the reader meets a confusing back-reference, not wrong information. It does land on the return-reward line, though. No qa contract covers it.

findings.title: The drop cap splits 239 opening sentences: '1 / 969년', '『스 / 무 편의…'
findings.where: public/book.css:100 (.lede.cap::first-letter), applied to author and work ledes
findings.impact: The first thing drawn on 239 pages is a broken year or a broken book title. On a phone the big digit reads as a separate '1'.
findings.fix: Add the cap class only when the first character is a Hangul syllable followed by more Hangul. Otherwise drop the cap.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. The rule `.lede.cap::first-letter{float:left;font-size:3.5em}` is at book.css:100. A scan of all 1,157 `p.lede.cap` found 180 that start with a digit, 32 with 『, 11 with ', 11 with 「, 3 with ‘, 1 with 《 and 1 with Latin ('POUM'). That is 239, matching the auditor. The screenshots show a giant '1' followed by '969년부터' on park-kyung-ni, and a giant '『스' followed by '무 편의…' on pablo-neruda. The 35 one-syllable Hangul cases, such as the giant '한' before '문장의' on Kafka's 변신, look like an ordinary drop cap. Only innerText and copy lose the space there, so those 35 are not a visible defect. The broken years and titles on 239 pages are real, and are the first thing drawn on those pages.

findings.title: The same work goes by two titles, sometimes on the same card or page
findings.where: relation summaries and significance fields against works[].titleKo
findings.impact: A reader cannot tell whether two titles are one book. On the Mo Yan page the heading looks like it names the film. The one-book promise depends on one name per book.
findings.fix: Normalise quoted titles in relation and significance text to titleKo, glossing the original only when it is needed. Add a validator warning when a quoted title is similar to, but not equal to, the author's titleKo.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. The front-page door for 도스토예프스키 lists '지하로부터의 수기' and the relation line '『지하생활자의 수기』 프랑스어 판본'. /authors/fyodor-dostoevsky/ shows both titles, and so does /authors/matsuo-basho/: the work is 오쿠로 가는 좁은 길 while the relations say 『오쿠노 호소미치』, and the author text says 발구 while a relation says 홋쿠. Relation summaries also say 카라마조프 가의 형제들, 보바리 부인, 베니스에서의 죽음, 헤다 가블러, 또 다른 심문 and 모르그 가의 살인 against the titleKo values. It is narrower than stated in two ways. Most variants are real alternative Korean edition titles (보바리 부인, 지하생활자의 수기), so a Korean reader usually recognises the same book. On Mo Yan, 붉은 수수밭 is the Korean edition's title, so the heading is correct; the significance just doesn't explain that the Korean edition carries the film's title. The Dostoevsky, Bashō and Mo Yan pages are genuinely confusing, but the consequence is small, so I downgraded it to low.

findings.title: The same person is spelled two ways across the corpus
findings.where: relation summaries and importanceReason fields against names.ko
findings.impact: Readers following a link find a different name on arrival, and the name search matches only the canonical form or listed aliases.
findings.fix: Use names.ko in prose. Add a check that flags Hangul aliases appearing in prose fields.

verdict.reason: Reproduced, and the Holmes case is sharper than stated. /authors/arthur-conan-doyle/ itself uses '홈즈' in its own text and '홈스' in its relations (Poe, Christie, Werber), so both spellings appear on one page. Wace's names.ko is 와스 but the Layamon sketch lede reads '바스의 프랑스어 『브뤼』'. Harivansh Rai Bachchan's lede has '우마르 하이얌'. Phaedrus and La Fontaine say '이솝', and the '버질 협회' line is drawn on the ts-eliot and virgil pages. Impact is lower than claimed. Every variant is already listed in that author's names.aliases, so the name search matches them. 이솝 is also the dominant Korean form, and '버질 협회' names an English institution. Only 홈즈/홈스 and 바스/와스 (바스 reads like Bath) are real reader-facing inconsistencies.

findings.title: Chinese and Japanese titles and English names/words dropped untranslated into Korean sentences, while other entries are glossed
findings.where: relation summaries (list in leak_han.txt and leak_latin.txt); work facts table (world.editions)
findings.impact: Korean phone readers get unreadable strings in the middle of the lines meant to earn their trust. Some of the untranslated books exist in Korean, for example 『酒国』 as 『술의 나라』.
findings.fix: Give every CJK or Latin title a Korean gloss, in the form already used for 終りし道の標に. Transliterate person names. Put titles in brackets.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. The relation summaries for dialogue--mo-yan--yu-hua, influence--william-faulkner--yu-hua, influence--lu-xun--yu-hua, translation--raymond-carver--haruki-murakami and the two Higashino affinities carry bare Simplified Chinese or Japanese titles. The Carver one is the featured '이어지는 한 사람' line on /authors/haruki-murakami/. The Latin strings 'H. B. Jassin의' (4 pages), 'bio-bibliography는' (4), 'the transatlantic review 콘래드' (2), '노벨문학위원 Anne Swärd는' (1) and 'Billy Budd, Sailor 는' are all drawn. The Botchan facts table shows '春陽堂, 東京' and 'ホトトギス発行所, 東京' unglossed, while Gitanjali glosses its Bengali publisher. One quote is misstated: the page reads '첫 장편 The Orchard Keeper(1965…' with no '는', though it is still unbracketed. Neither guide has a rule that requires a gloss, so this is an inconsistency and a readability cost. Most strings are secondary-source citations that a reader can skip, hence low.

findings.title: Developer and QC jargon on 656 work pages (API, SRU, MARC, 국중도, '입문작 판본 확인'), some of it in English or Japanese
findings.where: work pages, edition table rows tr.why and span.src (generate-static-pages.ts edition rendering; editions.json verifiedFrom and note)
findings.impact: First-time readers cannot parse these lines, and they break the page's 다체 register. The honesty signal ('we checked this') is buried under tool names.
findings.fix: Render the provenance in reader Korean, e.g. '국립중앙도서관 서지와 대조, 2026-09-24'. Keep tool names and QC phrases in the data, not on the page.

verdict.reason: The counts reproduce: 1,075 + 25 + 1 rows of '카카오 책 검색 API · 제목·저자·ISBN-13 대조' on 656 pages, 386 LoC SRU, 158 BnF SRU, 92 DNB SRU, 55 '国立国会図書館サーチ OpenSearch' and 4 'kakao book search (title query)'. '국중도' appears on 24 pages, MARC on 11, and '입문작 판본 확인' on 35 pages. That last figure is pages, not the auditor's 51 rows, and my scan did not check the row count. The line is narrower than 'developer jargon'. The `.src` span is a deliberate provenance stamp in 12px grey, and showing where a claim was checked serves the motto. The real problems are the opaque protocol names (SRU, OpenSearch, MARC, 국중도), the 4 English rows and the Japanese-only 55, and the QC memo '(2026-09-24 입문작 판본 확인, 서점 상품 페이지·역자 소개)' in the reader-facing note. It is readable but unpolished, so low rather than medium.

findings.title: Period and region names differ between the index and the front page's literacy map
findings.where: src/types.ts PERIOD_DEFS/REGION_DEFS (used by the index) vs public/atlas.js:241-254 REGION_KO/PERIOD_KO (front page)
findings.impact: The same period is called '21세기 후속층' in one place and '동시대' in another. A reader cannot connect the literacy map to the index filter it should lead to.
findings.fix: Use one label table. Import the types.ts labels into atlas.js through the build, or copy them exactly.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. The /authors/ filter options read '중기 현대문학 1930–1970', '21세기 후속층 1990–현재' and '사하라 이남 아프리카'. The front page's literacy map, when opened, reads '중기 현대 0/744', '동시대 0/486' and '사하라 이남 0/61'. The two tables are separate: atlas.js PERIOD_KO/REGION_KO against types.ts PERIOD_DEFS/REGION_DEFS. The only mismatch a reader cannot bridge is 동시대 against 21세기 후속층. The other two are abbreviations, and '21세기 후속층 1990–현재' is itself an odd label. Both surfaces use '뿌리층'. Low consequence.

findings.title: The sign-in box on every page says '도감 지키기' and never says it is email sign-in for syncing
findings.where: public/book.js:188-191 (paintAuth) and the success message at :198
findings.impact: A first-time reader sees a bare email field under an opaque verb phrase. They are asked for personal data without being told what for, which works against the 15-minute first-mark promise.
findings.fix: Label it plainly, e.g. '다른 기기에서도 이어 보기 — 이메일로 링크를 보낸다'. State what is stored in the same sentence.

verdict.reason: Reproduced at 390px on /authors/victor-hugo/. The page ends with an '이메일' field, a '도감 지키기' button and '저장은 어떤 책을 어느 칸에, 언제 — 그것뿐.'. There is no heading, and nothing says a sign-in link will be emailed or that the purpose is keeping marks across devices. '도감' appears in no other visible UI string. In atlas.js it is only in comments, and in book.js only in the sync and success messages. The footnote does say what is stored, which softens the privacy side. Still, an unexplained request for an email address on every page works against first-visit trust. Medium stands.

findings.title: Internal word '배치' (generation batch) appears in reader text
findings.where: relations: affinity--franz-kafka--samuel-beckett, affinity--george-orwell--albert-camus, influence--virginia-woolf--simone-de-beauvoir, contrast--zora-neale-hurston--ralph-ellison, influence--anton-chekhov--flannery-oconnor
findings.impact: Readers take '배치' to mean 'arrangement', so the hedging sentence is unintelligible. It exposes pipeline vocabulary on a page whose motto is honesty.
findings.fix: Replace it with '여기서는' or '이 책에서는'.

verdict.reason: Reproduced, and it is broader than reported. The 5 relation summaries are as listed, and 17 built pages contain '이 배치'. The auditor missed an author-level leak: naguib-mahfouz importanceReason is drawn on /authors/naguib-mahfouz/ as '…이 배치에서 그는 제국을 향해 되받아 쓰지 않은 쪽 —…', which is pipeline-batch vocabulary. chinua-achebe importanceReason also has '이 배치의 두 축' in the data, but it is not drawn on the page. Where 배치 means 'arrangement' it is fine: isidore-of-seville, don-delillo ('배치하는'), and imre-kertesz readingWarning.

findings.title: Reading-entry reason and entry-work significance, drawn back to back, repeat each other
findings.where: author pages ('여기서 읽기 시작' row) and front page lpWorks(withEntry). 20 plates have 10+ characters of shared text; list produced by the overlap script
findings.impact: Reads as machine-generated padding in the most important row of the page.
findings.fix: Rewrite the entry reasons for the 20 flagged plates so they say why to start there, not what the book is.

verdict.reason: Reproduced on the three pages I checked. On each, the reading-entry reason and the entry work's significance are drawn on consecutive lines with near-identical wording. I did not re-run the 20-plate overlap count.

findings.title: Aristotle's entry reason assumes the reader has already read Oedipus
findings.where: authors aristotle readingEntryReason (also sophocles), drawn on the author page and the front page
findings.impact: This is a leftover from a sequenced tour. A reader who arrives from the index has read nothing before.
findings.fix: Change '앞서 읽은' to '소포클레스의'.

verdict.reason: Reproduced on /authors/aristotle/. The parenthetical '(also sophocles)' is not borne out: Sophocles' fields contain no '앞서 읽은' or tour-sequence phrasing. A similar leftover exists in abai-qunanbaiuly readingWarning ('앞서 읽은 시들을…'), but in a 'next step' warning it is defensible.

findings.title: Register break: the only polite-form UI string, in the front page's failure message
findings.where: scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:1057
findings.impact: The mixed register shows up exactly when something fails.
findings.fix: Change it to '시도해 달라'.

verdict.reason: Reproduced with /atlas.js aborted in Playwright. #app shows the polite '해 주세요' in an otherwise 해라체 UI. The equivalent message in book.js sendErrorKo is '잠시 뒤에 다시 시도해 달라.'. It only appears when the page fails, so low.

findings.title: 'Not yet checked (checked on date)' contradicts itself on 3,498 work pages
findings.where: scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:312
findings.impact: '확인' right after 'not checked' reads as if the check happened. The intended meaning is 'as of that date'.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: 3,498 work pages carry exactly this sentence, generated at scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:312. '확인' straight after 'not checked yet' does read as a contradiction, and the intended meaning is 'as of that date'. The wording is locked in by a passing contract, qa/verify-book.mjs:245, whose regex requires '아직 검수하지 않았다 (YYYY-MM-DD 확인)'. The fix therefore has to change that contract too. This is not a duplicate: the contract guarantees the sentence is present, not that it reads correctly.

findings.title: Space before a particle or copula after brackets and Latin titles
findings.where: works natsume-soseki--botchan world.editions[1].note; franz-kafka--der-verschollene world.editions[0].note; rabindranath-tagore--nationalism world.written; herman-melville--billy-budd significance (2)
findings.impact: Visible spacing errors on work pages.
findings.fix: Remove the spaces. Add the regex to the validator.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. A regex over the extracted text of all author and work pages (a closing bracket or a Latin word, then a space, then a particle or copula) returns exactly these 5 instances and no others.

findings.title: Our own opening-sentence translations: '게다가' misreads, and a 「」 dialogue quote looks like a title
findings.where: works natsume-soseki--sorekara world.opening.ko; franz-kafka--in-der-strafkolonie world.opening.ko
findings.impact: The one line of self-translation on the page misparses.
findings.fix: Write '도마만 한 나막신(게다)이'. Use “ ” for dialogue.

verdict.reason: Both are drawn as described. '게다' (Japanese clog) is a standard-dictionary word, so '게다가' is grammatical, but a Korean reader will first parse it as the adverb 게다가 ('moreover'), which makes the line misread. The 「」 around dialogue on in-der-strafkolonie conflicts with editorial-guide.md:76, which reserves 「」 for short works and poems. It is the only one of 15 opening translations that uses 「」.

findings.title: Genre label '소설·단편' names a single novel's genre on 2,089 work pages; silhouette copy contradicts itself
findings.where: src/types.ts:509 GENRE_DEFS fiction ko; silhouette labels in generate-static-pages.ts and the front-page render()
findings.impact: The label reads as 'novel or short story' for a known novel. The silhouette labels say the opposite of what the page shows.
findings.fix: Use '소설' for the genre label on a single work. Align the silhouette label with the body text: '이름·자리·책만 안다'.

verdict.reason: The silhouette contradiction is real. /authors/f-scott-fitzgerald/ is labelled '실루엣 / 이름과 자리만 안다' but lists '책 3' and says '이 책들이 있다는 것과 언제 어느 말로 쓰였는지는 안다'. The front-page render() at generate-static-pages.ts:993 prints '이름과 자리만 안다. 이 사람의 쪽은 아직 비어 있다.' and then draws '여기서 읽기 시작한다면' with works. The genre half is weak. '소설·단편' is the category label for the fiction genre (GENRE_DEFS in types.ts), shown on 2,089 pages as a genre tag, and a Korean reader takes it as the category 'fiction (novels and stories)'. That half is close to a non-defect.

findings.title: Sampled machine-sounding sentences and a transcription error
findings.where: authors bernard-werber difficultyReason; works william-butler-yeats--the-wind-among-the-reeds significance; authors oodgeroo-noonuccal names.ko; works imre-kertesz--felszamolas edition note
findings.impact: Isolated. They are signs that the prose was only sampled, not read in full.

findings.title: 4 of 5 synthetic violations pass all 113 browser contracts. The Korean-edition contract counts English editions as Korean.
findings.where: qa/verify-book.mjs:245-248 (추정 check reads one row), :350-384 (sitemap/noindex checks, no reviewStatus for work pages), :620-626 (Korean-edition check), :150-158 (sign-in: no merge check)
findings.impact: The contracts guarantee less than their names say. A build that hands a first-time reader an author with no Korean book, drops 「추정」 on every translation-basis cell but one, submits 794 unreviewed pages to search engines, or silently never uploads a reader's marks would go green and deploy. That covers the product promise (a book to mark within 15 minutes), the motto (그 판정은 추정이다), and the reviewed-only indexing policy.
findings.fix: Make the Korean-edition check read the 「한국어 N」 group, not any 「검수된 판본」. Assert FIRST equals the graph-derived list. Check the 추정 labels against qc/edition-basis.json for every row. Derive indexability from data reviewStatus for every page. Add a signed-in browser contract that asserts marks_merge receives the local marks.

verdict.reason: I reproduced all four with my own mutation script on fresh copies of the frozen dist, repo qa/ and data/. All four stayed green at 113/113. The Korean-edition contract uses the regex /검수된 판본 \d+/, which also matches a table that holds only an English original, so under a synthetic violation it passes vacuously. That is a real defect in what CI claims to guarantee. I downgraded it from high: no reader-facing page is wrong today, and it is a gap in future protection.

findings.title: The 「도감 지키기」 sign-in on all 6,097 pages cannot work for ordinary readers, and the rate-limit message blames the reader
findings.where: public/book.js:188-211; docs/backend-design.md:22,153; STATUS.md:41
findings.impact: Every Korean reader sees an offer to keep their 도감 that fails for anyone outside the team. The fallback text is honest about this. When the shared hourly quota is used up (possibly by other apps), the reader is told *they* sent too many emails, which is false. Each attempt also posts create_user:true to a shared auth pool. If SMTP is added, first-time users still get English 'Confirm your signup' mail (mailer_autoconfirm=false), and site_url points at another app.
findings.fix: Hide the form until custom SMTP is attached and a Korean template is set, or say plainly that it is a closed test. Reword the 429 message to 「지금은 메일을 보낼 수 없다」 without blaming the reader.

verdict.reason: The core claim holds. All 6,097 pages carry #lp-auth and /book.js, and paintAuth unhides an email form. SMTP is not configured and the project records that the default mailer may not deliver outside the team, so the offer is dead for ordinary readers. The rejection text it shows is honest. Overstated: the 429 text is subjectless Korean (「메일을 너무 자주 보냈다」). It is ambiguous and can be read as blaming the reader, but it does not name the reader. I did not observe the team-only delivery rule directly. It is inferred from Supabase behaviour, the code comment and STATUS.md.

findings.title: Any link carrying #access_token silently signs the reader into that account and uploads all their local marks to it
findings.where: public/book.js:84-97 (absorbCallback), 155-171, 244-260
findings.impact: Someone who sends a crafted link gets the victim's whole reading list, plus every later mark (lpSet mirrors to the server), by reading their own account. This is latent today because getting tokens needs a deliverable magic link (team-only mailer). It becomes live the day SMTP is attached, which STATUS.md lists as the next step.
findings.fix: Switch to PKCE (flow_type=pkce: code in the query, verifier stored when the email is requested) or at least absorb tokens only when this browser has a pending-login nonce. Show the signed-in email address.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly. absorbCallback (book.js:84-97) accepts any #access_token with no nonce or PKCE, and syncOnLoad then uploads every local mark under that token. I downgraded it because it is latent. An attacker needs valid tokens for their own account, which requires a deliverable magic link, and the default mailer does not deliver to outsiders. The data exposed is a reading list.

findings.title: deploy.sh ships a local build that CI never built or verified, and untracked data or public files go with it
findings.where: scripts/deploy.sh:9,24-25; scripts/lib/load-node.ts:13; scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:1183
findings.impact: An untracked data/authors/*.json, a data/works file, or a stray public/ asset (including gitignored ones such as .DS_Store) reaches production under a green CI that never saw it. 'CI 가 초록일 때만' guarantees the commit, not the artifact. No such file exists today (public/ has 315 tracked = 315 on disk).
findings.fix: Build from a clean export (`git worktree add`/`git archive HEAD`) or fail on any untracked or ignored file under data/ and public/. Better still, deploy CI's own verified dist as an artifact.

verdict.reason: deploy.sh:9 ignores untracked files. deploy.sh:23-24 builds locally and ships with --commit-dirty=true without running verify:book on that artifact. load-node.ts reads every *.json in data/<dir>, and the generator cpSyncs public/. So files CI never saw can ship under a green CI. No such file exists today, but agents write batch files into data/, so the path is realistic.

findings.fix: Embed a build id (commit sha plus a content hash of all of dist) in a meta tag or /build.txt and compare that.

verdict.reason: The walk hash covers names only, so for any deploy that leaves author names unchanged, the live check matches the previous deployment. The consequence is small. `wrangler pages deploy` is synchronous and exits non-zero on failure under set -e, so the only thing this check can miss is a stalled or rolled-back deployment. I downgraded it from medium.

findings.title: A mid-week deploy changes 'this week's page' for readers with no marks. On 2026-09-24 week 39 switched from 조르주 페렉 to 최인훈.
findings.where: public/atlas.js:210-214 (firstOpen), generate-static-pages.ts FIRST list

findings.where: public/book.js:155-171 (syncOnLoad saves a merge of the pre-fetch local snapshot)
findings.impact: On slow phone networks, a signed-in reader's first tap on a page visibly undoes itself. If they are offline afterwards, the mark is gone locally.
findings.fix: Re-read local state after the fetch and merge that, or merge per-key against the latest localStorage.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. syncOnLoad snapshots local state before the fetch and saves the merge afterwards (book.js:160-164), overwriting a mark made in between. The stamp visibly un-presses.

findings.title: Auth failures are silent or destructive: sign-out doesn't revoke the session; a 503/429 on refresh signs the reader out; offline refresh throws uncaught; expired links and blocked storage give no message
findings.impact: A transient server error or a hit on the shared rate limit forces a new magic link, which costs one of 2 emails per hour for four apps. A reader returning from an expired or blocked link sees nothing happen. On a shared device the next person's sign-in merges the previous reader's marks.
findings.fix: POST /auth/v1/logout on sign-out and offer to clear local marks. Remove the session only on 400/401 invalid_grant. Wrap session() in try and paint 'failed'. Show a message for #error= and for unsaved sessions.

verdict.reason: Each sub-claim reproduced. I checked blocked storage only statically: save() swallows the error, then replaceState erases the hash.

findings.title: A signed-in user can write unbounded rows and future timestamps into the shared 500 MB database
findings.where: supabase/migrations/20260903000001_book.sql (grants, marks_merge), 20260923000001_book_tombstones.sql
findings.impact: One account could fill the free-plan DB shared by four apps. A device with a wrong clock wins every later edit from other devices forever. Latent while sign-in is team-only.
findings.fix: Revoke direct insert on mark_events (write only via mark_set). Cap the array length in marks_merge. Clamp p_at to now() + small skew. Add a per-user row cap.

verdict.reason: From the migrations: authenticated users can insert into mark_events directly, marks_merge loops over an unbounded jsonb array, and p_at is never clamped. The client merge lets a future server timestamp win permanently. It is latent while sign-in is effectively team-only. I did not check the deployed function bodies against the migrations.

findings.title: The front page's h() escaper does not escape quotes but is used in attribute values
findings.where: scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:962 (h), lpControl data-t/data-a, <option value>, img alt
findings.impact: The first work title or Korean name with a double quote would break the mark control's data-t (shelf title) or the datalist markup. No exploitable path was found (all ids are slug-validated).
findings.fix: Use an escaper that also replaces " (like the generator's esc), or set attributes via DOM APIs.

verdict.reason: h() is a textContent/innerHTML round trip that does not escape ". It is used inside the option value, the img alt, and the data-t and data-a attributes. Today no Korean name or work title contains a quote, so nothing renders wrong. This is a latent hazard with no validate-data guard. All text-position uses do go through h(), including the julio-cortazar summary containing '<'.

findings.title: The door's name normaliser is broken by template-literal escaping: it doesn't remove spaces, and it deletes every 's' and every digit
findings.where: scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:1090 (inside a TS template literal); built output dist/index.html, function lpNorm
findings.impact: Korean readers on phones often type foreign names without spaces. For about a third of the full-entry authors, that is answered with 'not found' or a list, and for some other authors it opens the wrong person. Any title or name made only of digits (1984, 2666) or of letters the normaliser strips produces a list of four unrelated authors.
findings.fix: Double the backslashes at line 1090 (`[\\s·.,\\-_'’]`), as lines 965-969 already do. Add a contract that types a no-space name (e.g. 조지오웰) and a dotted-initial name.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently. The built lpNorm is `replace(/[s·.,-_'’]/g,'')` (od -c on dist/index.html). The `,-_` range (0x2C–0x5F) takes out digits and punctuation, the letter s is removed, and whitespace is kept. The source at scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:1090 has a single-escaped `\s` inside the TS template. My own replica, which evals lpNorm straight from the built HTML, gives exactly the auditor's figures: of 1,540 no-space Korean names, 618 ok, 523 miss, 305 list and 94 wrong, and 60 plates fail. With the intended normaliser all 1,540 pass. In Chrome at 390x844, '조지오웰' shows '이 이름으로는 찾지 못했다' and '1984' shows the list '라빈드라나트 타고르 · 나쓰메 소세키 · 루쉰 · 아쿠타가와 류노스케'. The list is the first four of all 193 plates, because the empty string matches every key. The only door contract (qa/verify-book.mjs ~l.607) types '도스토예프스키', an exact stored alias, so it never exercises the normaliser. Nuance: removing the letter s is symmetric, so it rarely breaks English names by itself. The damage comes from spaces not being removed and from digits and dots being stripped. 'C.S. 루이스' and 'T.S. 엘리엇' miss, while 'C. S. 루이스' opens.

findings.title: Near-miss names silently open a different author, with nothing telling the reader the page is a guess
findings.where: dist/index.html door submit handler (source scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:1082-1085): substring match plus 'same first 3 characters, length within ±2', then 'keep only plates if any plate matched', then 'open if one is left'
findings.impact: This breaks the motto directly: instead of saying 'we don't have 오스카 와일드', the door presents a Bolivian poet as the answer. A reader who doesn't know the substitute's face may believe it, or mark a book by the wrong author.
findings.fix: Only exact (normalised) matches should open a page directly. Any fuzzy match should become a '혹시 이 사람?' list that says the typed name itself was not found.

verdict.reason: Reproduced all 26 wrong opens with an independent replica. I drove 12 of them in Chrome and each one landed on the wrong author with #miss empty: 무라카미 류→하루키, 오스카 와일드→오스카르 세루토, 노자→스피노자, 해리 포터→해리 마르틴손, 공자→공자진, 에밀 졸라→에밀 시오란, 조지프 브로드스키→조지프 콘래드, 안나 카레니나→안나 아흐마토바, Jose Saramago→조지프 콘래드, and others. The screenshot shows the input '오스카 와일드' and, under '책의 한 쪽', the heading 오스카르 세루토 / Óscar Cerruto / 1912–1981 · 스페인어. Nothing tells the reader the page is a guess. The cause is the fuzzy step: a substring match or the same first 3 characters within ±2 length, then an automatic open when exactly one plate is left. This is independent of door-01. 무라카미류 still reaches 하루키 under the intended normaliser. Presenting an unrelated person as the answer contradicts the motto directly. Minor error: 루이스 캐럴 opens 루이스 맥니스, not '루이 맥니스'. The claim that 1Q84 hides 하루키 is real but is caused by door-01 (digits stripped, '1q84'→'q').

findings.title: The front page claims the whole world is already here, but the Korean school canon, Korea's bestselling novelists and mass-read foreign classics are missing, and the page never says so
findings.where: dist/index.html:97 lede '세계는 처음부터 전부 여기 있고, 아직 만나지 않은 이름은 실루엣으로 서 있다'; docs/one-book.md ('세계문학 전부가 처음부터 지도에 있고'; '범위는 데이터 주장이다'); miss text '이 이름으로는 찾지 못했다'
findings.impact: The product's entrance fails the most likely first names a Korean reader types (the textbook writers and this decade's bestsellers). The page states a completeness claim that is false, and it words each absence as a search failure, which makes the reader retry spellings. That contradicts '없는 것은 없다고 적는다', which the project's own docs apply to scope ('범위는 데이터 주장이다').
findings.fix: Remove or qualify the lede's completeness claim, or make it true. When there is no exact or fuzzy match at all, say plainly '이 책에는 아직 「X」가 없다'. Rebalance intake toward Korean modern and contemporary writers and the Japanese and Chinese fiction Korean readers actually buy.

verdict.reason: All 20 named Korean writers are absent from the names, the aliases and the index data-h. Korean-language authors number 36: 26 plates and 10 sketches, all Joseon-era. English is 506, Japanese 42, born 1950 or later 109 (17 of them plates). All seven Nobel absentees are confirmed: '밥 딜런' and 'Bob Dylan' miss, the only Dylan in the data is Dylan Thomas, and '루이즈 글릭' gives a list of 루이즈 라베 and 루이즈 어드리크. Modern Chinese: 라오서, 바진, 선충원, 쑤퉁, 옌롄커, 류츠신 and 金庸 are absent, while 위화, 모옌, 루쉰 and 장아이링 are present. The lede on dist/index.html reads '모든 책을 품은 하나의 책. 세계는 처음부터 전부 여기 있고, 아직 만나지 않은 이름은 실루엣으로 서 있다'. docs/one-book.md:5 says '세계문학 전부가 처음부터 지도에 있고', but only 2 silhouettes exist, so the completeness claim is false as a data claim ('범위는 데이터 주장이다', one-book.md:19). A passing contract enshrines the '못 찾았다' wording on purpose (verify-book.mjs: '없는 이름에는 「없다」가 아니라 「못 찾았다」'). This finding therefore challenges a deliberate design choice rather than a bug, but the honesty gap is real. Two evidence details are slightly off. The Kyobo phrase 'four Korean novelists … at #1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8' is garbled: the list has six Korean novels in its top 10, with 한강 at #1 and #2 and 불편한 편의점 at #5 and 달러구트 at #6 confirmed. The 43.8% Japan share is all genres including comics, which the auditor itself caveats, so the Japan gap is overstated in size but right in direction.

verdict.reason: The index dead-ends are real and confirmed in Chrome. /authors/?q= returns '「…」에 맞는 이름이 없다' for 애거서 크리스티, 아가사 크리스티, 조지오웰, Dostoyevsky, 어린왕자, 상실의 시대, 세익스피어 and C.S. 루이스, while '어린 왕자' and '채식주의자' do find their author. Christie is a plate stored with no aliases (['agatha-christie','애거사 크리스티','Agatha Christie','p']). The book's own edition row prints '『애크로이드 살인사건(애거서 크리스티 추리문학 베스트 7)』'. Two parts are narrower than stated. First, the index sentence literally says that no name matches the typed string, which is true as a string match. The harm is that a reader takes it as 'the book has no such person', and the trailing '책 제목이나 원어 이름으로도 찾는다' sends them to retry. That is misleading rather than a flat falsehood. Second, 'Five authors … reached by none of the variants' only reflects the auditor's variants. The stored display forms 'C. S. 루이스', 'T. S. 엘리엇' and '요시프 브로드스키' open the right person at the door. What fails are the dotted forms without a space (door-01) and the common Korean spellings that aren't stored.

findings.title: The door never matches work titles, even for books it carries, and some titles open the wrong author
findings.where: dist/index.html door submit handler: keys are only author name, original name and aliases (x[1], x[2], x[4])
findings.impact: Many Korean readers remember the book rather than the author. The door asks for an author name (placeholder '좋아한 작가 이름'), so this is one extra tap rather than a dead end, except for the wrong opens and the digit titles.
findings.fix: Include work titles from walk/works data as keys that route to the author, or at least stop fuzzy matching titles to names.

verdict.reason: It is true that the door keys only on name, original name and aliases (x[1], x[2], x[4]). 채식주의자, 데미안, 어린 왕자, 안나카레니나 and 해리포터 all miss or send the reader to the index, and the index then finds several of them (채식주의자→한강, 어린 왕자→생텍쥐페리). But the door explicitly asks for an author (placeholder '좋아한 작가 이름'), and the miss path hands off to the index, which searches titles. So title-only misses are a design limit costing one tap, not a defect. The serious parts restate other findings: the wrong opens by title (안나 카레니나→아흐마토바, 제인 에어→오스틴, 해리 포터→마르틴손) are door-02, and the digit titles (1984, 2666, 1Q84) are door-01.

findings.title: The door's suggestion list offers only the 193 plates, so 1,644 sketch authors, including Stephen King, Krasznahorkai and Charlotte Brontë, are never suggested

Datalist support on mobile is patchy, the exact name still opens a sketch ('스티븐 킹' and '스티븐킹' both open stephen-king), and the plate-preference harm is already counted in door-02.

Method limits:
- The year test only asks whether the same number appears anywhere in the Wikipedia text, so it cannot catch a correct year attached to the wrong event.
- Entailment in (B) was judged by one rater (me). Wikipedia pages were read at their current revision, which may differ from the ledger's read date.

findings.title: Tom Sawyer is set in a 'Missouri riverside village' (미주리 강가 마을), on the week-48 front card and under the red seal. The ledger confirmed it with a quote that says the Mississippi.
findings.where: data/works/silhouette-wave1.json:19514 (mark-twain--the-adventures-of-tom-sawyer significance); rendered on /works/mark-twain--the-adventures-of-tom-sawyer/, on /authors/mark-twain/ (red seal), and in dist/walk/mark-twain.json, which drives the week-48 no-mark front card. Ledger: qc/closeread/plate-wave1.json:8684
findings.impact: Every reader with no marks sees this card in ISO week 48 (firstOpen(FIRST,48,0) = 'mark-twain'), under a red 'reviewed' seal. It contradicts the author's own lede. It also shows the gate confirming a claim its own quote contradicts.
findings.fix: Change to '미주리주의 미시시피 강가 마을' and reopen the ledger claim.

verdict.reason: I reproduced this. On the frozen build, the Tom Sawyer significance line reads '미주리 강가 마을의 소년기를…'. Most Korean readers will take that as a village on the Missouri River. The novel's St. Petersburg is a Mississippi River town (modelled on Hannibal, Missouri). The ledger marks the claim confirmed even though its own quote says 'Mississippi River'. The same card's WHY line says '미시시피 강가 소년', so a reader sees the two lines disagree on one card. I recomputed firstOpen from a copy of dist/atlas.js: week 48, turn 0 is mark-twain. The index.html pageHtml renders the works list with each work's .s line, so every reader with no marks sees this sentence that week, and mark-twain is in the sitemap's reviewed 38. I downgraded it from high: it is a one-word geographic slip, and '미주리' can also be read as the state name. It is still a real error under the red seal and a real gate false-accept.

findings.title: The site says Eliot called Baudelaire 'the first poet to make urban ugliness the material of poetry'. Eliot's 1930 essay says the opposite ('not merely ...').
findings.where: data/relations/rel-early-canon.json:700 (influence--charles-baudelaire--ts-eliot, evidenceLevel documented). Rendered on /authors/charles-baudelaire/ (week-47 turn-0 author), /authors/ts-eliot/, /works/charles-baudelaire--les-fleurs-du-mal/ and /works/ts-eliot--the-waste-land/.
findings.impact: A superlative is invented and attributed to a real critic's text, then labelled 'documented'. It is repeated on 4 pages, including the author who opens for every no-mark reader in week 47. It breaks the motto of not making things up.
findings.fix: Rewrite it as what Eliot says: Baudelaire raised the imagery of the sordid metropolis 'to the first intensity' and was 'the first counter-romantic in poetry'. Add a page-level source.

verdict.reason: I reproduced this. The relation summary says Eliot's 1930 introduction called Baudelaire '도시의 추악함을 시의 재료로 만든 최초의 시인'. The essay text says the opposite: 'It is not merely in the use of imagery of common life, not merely in the use of imagery of the sordid life of a great metropolis, but in the elevation of such imagery to the first intensity…'. The only 'first' Eliot gives him is 'the first counter-romantic in poetry'. A superlative is attributed to a named primary text and labelled documented. The only source record has no URL. The sentence ships on 4 HTML pages, in walk/charles-baudelaire.json and in graph.json. One correction to the finding: the week-47 no-mark front card does not render hops (pageHtml shows only why and works), so the sentence is one tap away on /authors/charles-baudelaire/, not on the card itself. That still makes it a high-severity honesty defect.

findings.title: The red-seal gate confirms claims its quotes do not support: 6/119 strict false-accepts (5.0%, CI 2.3–10.6%) and 23/119 (19.3%, CI 13.2–27.3%) counting partial entailment.
findings.where: qc/closeread/plate-wave1.json (lines 164, 2039, 2104/11472, 4385, 13189) plus the Twain claim at 8684; full list in /tmp/onebook-audit-0924/gap-gap-reviewed-and-weekly-plates-unverified/b_sample.json (field 'judge').

At least one false accept (#73) left a live factual error on a weekly page. The seal's 'reviewed' promise is weaker than the ledger totals suggest.

verdict.reason: The items I rechecked reproduce, but the headline rate overstates factual risk. Two not-entailing cases stand. The Glissant quote (on 'créolitude', 1977) does not support the sentence '세대적 대립축'. The quote-absent cases are also real: the id.wikisource Chairil page has no '1949' and no 'Mutiara', and the ru.wikisource Vremya 1862 page does not contain the quoted Dostoevsky sentence. findings.title: Living-person breach (Don DeLillo): he explicitly hedged that he had not yet read Ulysses; the site says he did. It also adds an unsupported causal claim and an uncited 'several interviews' claim about Beckett.

Rendered on /authors/don-delillo/, /authors/james-joyce/ (week-49 turn-0 author) and /authors/samuel-beckett/. don-delillo is in FIRST (week 42 turn 2).

verdict.reason: The Joyce part is real. In the full Paris Review interview, DeLillo credits Joyce for language's 'radiance' and then hedges: 'maybe I hadn't gotten to Ulysses at that point, it was Portrait of the Artist'. The site instead states flatly that he learned it from reading Ulysses. The follow-on causal sentence about brand names and broadcast voices is editorial inference presented as fact under a 'documented' label. The Beckett part is misstated in the finding. The auditor read a paywalled Wayback excerpt, only about 10k characters and 7 exchanges. The full 2012 snapshot does mention Beckett once, as 'Kafka's private vision and maybe Beckett's… a kind of world narrative'. That still does not support the site's claim that DeLillo repeatedly named Beckett as the writer who changed his generation's language. The Beckett relation is already scholarly_consensus, not documented. I did not check DeLillo's other interviews for the 'several times' claim.

findings.where: data/works/mid-south-a.json:22; rendered on /works/jorge-luis-borges--historia-universal-de-la-infamia/ and in the sig on /authors/jorge-luis-borges/ (FIRST pool, draft).

verdict.reason: I reproduced this. The Historia universal de la infamia (1935) significance line calls it '첫 산문집'. In Korean, 산문집 usually means an essay collection, and Borges had already published the essay books Inquisiciones (1925), El tamaño de mi esperanza (1926), El idioma de los argentinos (1928), Evaristo Carriego (1930) and Discusión (1932). It was his first book of narrative prose. The claim is false, but it sits on a draft plate, is not on any weekly turn-0 card, and is a single phrase, so I rated it low.

findings.title: iOS Safari readers who come back 'a week later' lose every mark with no warning beforehand, and the site offers no working way to keep them
findings.where: All pages: public/book.js, public/atlas.js and the inline runtime in scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:122-160 store everything in localStorage only. dist has no manifest, no service worker and no navigator.storage.persist (0 of 6,097 pages).
findings.impact: The one-sentence contract is 'mark one book in 15 minutes, come back on your own a week later'. The site's own weekly rotation (atlas.js isoWeek, 'this week's page') invites a same-weekday return, which is day 7, exactly the WebKit boundary. A reader who uses Safari daily and returns on day 8-10 finds an empty shelf and a stranger's greeting. That includes the weekly author choice (lp.seen.v1) and even the sign-in session (lp.session.v1). Nothing warned them beforehand. The promise fails on the platform the product was meant to be measured on.
findings.fix:
Warn before the loss, not after. Either:
- state the 7-day condition wherever the site says 이 기록은 이 브라우저 안에 있다 and on the first mark; or
- ship a manifest and a home-screen invitation (the exemption) and call navigator.storage.persist().
Then do the owner's real-iPhone 7-day test before relying on sign-in as the rescue.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is real. Every mark lives only in localStorage, and dist has no manifest, no service worker, no persist() call and no home-screen path. WebKit's primary post deletes all script-writable storage after seven days of Safari use without interaction on the site, and only home-screen apps are exempt. When storage is cleared, the shelf and the front page both fall back to the first-visit state, with no warning beforehand. I downgraded it from critical for three reasons. (1) It needs 7 or more days of Safari use with no tap on the site, so a reader who comes back after only 5-6 use-days, or who taps mid-week, keeps the marks. (2) Android Chrome and Samsung Internet readers, the majority of Korean phones, are not affected. (3) The project already records the risk in history.md:214. The fix as written is partly wrong. WebKit blog 14403 grants persist() only on heuristics such as being a home-screen web app, and it describes persistence as protection from storage-pressure eviction, not clearly from the ITP 7-day deletion. So calling persist() from Safari would not rescue the ordinary Safari reader. Only the home-screen route or a warning would help.

findings.title: Marks made in the KakaoTalk, Naver, Instagram or LINE in-app browser never appear in Safari or Chrome, even the same day, and the site neither detects this nor says so
findings.where: No in-app detection anywhere in dist (0 hits for KAKAOTALK, NAVER(inapp, Instagram, openExternal, openExternalBrowser, userAgent). Shelf copy at generate-static-pages.ts:805/830/838.
findings.impact: The common Korean path is: a link shared in KakaoTalk, marked in the in-app browser, then a return a week later from Safari, Chrome or the home screen. That reader finds nothing, on day 0 or any other day. Inside the in-app WKWebView, ITP is also on by default (webkit.org/blog/10882), so even a return through KakaoTalk is at risk after 7 days of app use (not verified on a device). Sign-in cannot rescue these marks either: the magic link opens in the mail app's browser, never back inside KakaoTalk (see the magic-link finding).
findings.fix: Detect in-app user agents and say, at the first mark, that marks made here stay inside this app. Offer an 'open in browser' action: kakaotalk://web/openExternal?url= for KakaoTalk, ?openExternalBrowser=1 for LINE, and an instruction for the others.

verdict.reason: Two parts are real. The site has no in-app detection and no 'open in browser' path (0 hits for KAKAOTALK, openExternal or userAgent). And the KakaoTalk in-app browser is an embedded WebView with its own storage. Kakao's own Android user agent carries the '; wv' WebView token, which is stronger evidence than the auditor's inference, and on iOS it lacks Version/ and is a WKWebView. So a mark made inside KakaoTalk is not in Safari or Chrome. The rest is narrower than stated. 'Never appear… even the same day' is derived from platform docs, not measured on any device. The Naver, Instagram and LINE claims are unverified per app. The most natural week-later return for a KakaoTalk-shared link is the same chat link, which reopens the same in-app store, and whether that store survives 7 days is unknown. The two-context Playwright analogue only shows that separate storages don't share, which is true by construction. What is solid is that the site never says 'this browser' can mean KakaoTalk's browser. That is a medium defect, not high.

findings.title: '링크를 열면 이 도감이 서버에 남는다' is false whenever the mail link opens in a different browser storage than the one holding the marks

verdict.reason: I reproduced it. The session is written only where the link lands (absorbCallback, book.js:84-97), and syncOnLoad merges only that storage's local marks. When the link is opened in a different storage, context A's mark is never sent. A stays signed out, and B reports '도감이 서버에도 있다.' over an empty doc. Meanwhile A was told '링크를 열면 이 도감이 서버에 남는다'. I downgraded it from high because, under the default mailer, only pre-authorized team addresses receive the email at all, so today this reaches the team only, not general readers. findings.title: In real Safari and Chrome private mode, marks appear to save, with no error, and then vanish; the error copy and its qa contract cover only a throwing mode modern private browsing does not produce
findings.where: scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:144-148 (mark-err shows only when lpSave returns false); qa/verify-book.mjs:663-673 (the contract forces localStorage to throw)
findings.impact: A reader in a Safari private tab, Chrome Incognito or Samsung secret mode marks a book, sees the red 「관심 있는 책」 and '서재에 꽂혔다', and loses it when the tab closes. In Safari it is not even visible in a second private tab. The one sentence that names private mode never appears to the readers it describes.
findings.fix: Detect ephemeral storage where possible (e.g. navigator.storage.estimate quota heuristics, or a sessionStorage/localStorage probe across tabs), or state the private-mode loss as a plain condition next to the shelf copy rather than as an error that fires only on a throw. Rewrite the qa contract to assert the sentence a real private-mode reader sees.

verdict.reason: Several things are true. Modern Safari private browsing does not throw; per WebKit changeset 215315 its localStorage is ephemeral and per-tab. An ephemeral context shows no mark-err and loses the mark. And the error sentence's mention of '사생활 보호 모드' names a cause that no longer throws. But the qa contract does not pass vacuously. The throwing path is real whenever site data or cookies are blocked, and the copy names that case too ('사이트 데이터 차단'), so the contract guards a live branch. Losing data when a private tab closes is the behaviour private-mode users expect, so the harm to a reader is small. My Playwright 'private' test is only a fresh context, not real Incognito or Safari private, which also applies to the auditor's run. The real defect is small: the sentence misattributes the cause, and private-mode readers get no hint. Severity low, not high.

findings.where: scripts/generate-static-pages.ts:805, 830, 831, 838, 867; public/book.js:191, 197; docs/backend-design.md:140 (the reader sentence the design prescribed)
