findings.title: On iPhone Safari, WebKit may delete a reader's marks before the promised week-later return, and readers cannot use the sign-in that was meant to protect against this
findings.where: dist/book.js:174,205-210; dist/shelf/index.html ('이 기록은 이 브라우저 안에 있다'); docs/backend-design.md:134,153,173-181; docs/one-sentence-contract.md:3-4
findings.impact: Consider an iPhone reader who marks 「관심 있는 책」 and uses Safari on 7 or more days without opening the site. Their marks, and the atlas's seen/turn state, can be deleted: the shelf comes back empty and the front page treats them as a new reader. That breaks the second half of the one-sentence contract ('일주일 뒤 스스로 돌아온다') for the iPhone share of the audience. The failed-sign-in message then tells the reader '표시는 이 기기에 그대로 있다', which on WebKit is not guaranteed, against the '지어내지 않는다' motto. The server-side fix the design relies on is unavailable to everyone outside the project team. This comes from documented policy and has not been observed on a device.
findings.fix: Stop claiming the marks are safe on iOS until they are. Change '표시는 이 기기에 그대로 있다' and '이 기록은 이 브라우저 안에 있다' to state the Safari 7-day condition, or suggest adding the site to the home screen and ship a manifest so that path is real. Either configure a production SMTP sender so sign-in works for readers, or change backend-design.md §4.5 so it no longer says the problem is closed. Run the pending 7-day iPhone test.

verdict.reason: The underlying risk is real. Marks live only in localStorage. dist ships no manifest or apple-mobile-web-app metadata. The frozen code's own comment says the default mailer sends only to project-team addresses, so the server copy that backend-design.md §4.5 says 'closes' the Safari 7-day problem is not available to ordinary readers. That doc also lists the iPhone 7-day test as pending in §8. Three parts are overstated. (1) Nothing was observed on a device. The loss needs 7 days of Safari use without visiting the site, which sits at the edge of a weekly return, so it is a risk and not a demonstrated failure. (2) The 'dishonest copy' charge does not hold: '이 기록은 이 브라우저 안에 있다' and '표시는 이 기기에 그대로 있다' are both true when they are shown. The honesty gap is in the design doc, where §4.5 says the problem is closed and §8 of the same file says it is open. It is not in reader-facing text. (3) supabase/config.toml is local-dev config and proves nothing about the hosted project's SMTP. The evidence for team-only mail is the comment at book.js:204. High is too much for a documented, unobserved platform-policy risk that the project already tracks as open.

findings.title: 『나는 고양이로소이다』 '초판 표지' is actually the 1906 English translation (I AM A CAT, tr. K. Ando)

findings.title: Signatures presented as the author's own hand whose file pages give no origin, a date after the signer's death, or an explicit doubt
findings.where: authors/{isaac-babel, gustave-flaubert, walt-whitman, joseph-conrad, william-faulkner, cesar-vallejo, premchand, pablo-neruda, sadegh-hedayat, luigi-pirandello}/ and the natsume-soseki mark
findings.impact: Each image makes a factual claim: this is the author's own hand. For 11 of the 62 the file page cannot back that claim. Babel's is an unsourced 2025 upload, and three dates fall after the signer's death, which points to a posthumous facsimile or a wrong date. The shelf of signatures carries more confidence than its sources support.
findings.fix: For signatures, require a named facsimile or archival source with a date inside the signer's life before shipping. Drop or replace Babel. Where the date is posthumous, say the image is a facsimile, or find a better file.

verdict.reason: The quoted wikitext is accurate for all the files I re-fetched: Flaubert date=1887; Whitman Date=1902-09-13 from Heritage; Conrad Date=1925 from Heritage; Faulkner's note about the signature machine, citing the NYT; Premchand's empty Source and Date; Neruda's vandalised description and blog source; Hedayat's 2024 Facebook source; Pirandello's 'Personal collection'. Babel is date=2025-01-15, source {{own}}, with no origin given. The inference is overstated, though. On Commons the Date field often records the document, sale or book date, not the moment of signing. A 1925 Conrad date or a 1902 Whitman sale date does not show that the signature is a facsimile. None of these file pages disputes attribution. What is true is narrower: for roughly 10 of the 62 signatures and marks, the file page gives weak or no traceable origin, and Babel's gives none. The site renders them as '<name>의 서명' with no source. This is a provenance-strength gap, not a demonstrated misattribution. I did not re-fetch the Natsume mark page. The shipped crop does show 漱石 plus seals, which is a legitimate 落款.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. The Strafkolonie image is plainly the printed title page (FRANZ KAFKA / IN DER STRAFKOLONIE / 1919 / KURT WOLFF VERLAG, LEIPZIG), but the alt text says '초판 표지'. The Botchan image shows 夏目漱石著 / 鶉籠 / 春陽堂 in seal script with an NDL stamp, which looks like a title leaf too, and its alt text says '『도련님』 초판 표지'. findings.impact: The caption tells readers the photo is PD-text, which is a category error. The photographer's rights in the photo are unstated. The photographer licensed his sibling photos CC BY 3.0.

verdict.reason: The file page does give Author '© Foto H.-P.Haack' with Permission {{PD-text}} and no separate licence for the photo. The rendered caption reads '사진 PD-text'. Calling it a category error is fair, because PD-text describes the depicted cover, not the photograph. Commons nonetheless hosts the file on that basis, treating the photo of a flat typographic wrapper as a reproduction. The manifest's licenceBasis states that reasoning explicitly. This is a wording and labelling issue, not an unrecorded rights problem.

findings.title: commercialUse flags are wrong or undecided on shipped images, and one credit line leaks internal English notes
findings.where: dist/art/manifest.json (3 'unknown', 8 'unverified-outside-source-jurisdiction'); authors/rabindranath-tagore and authors/natsume-soseki credit lines
findings.impact: The project ships images whose own ledger says they have not been cleared, and it never records the clearance. That is mostly a paperwork gap, since Korea's term for authors who died before 1963 has expired, but it is not tracked. Korean readers see raw internal English notes in the credit line.
findings.fix: Resolve each flag to yes or no with a one-line Korean-jurisdiction basis. Render a short licence name, not the manifest's free-text licence string.

verdict.reason: The counts are accurate: 3 'unknown' (Pessoa CC0, Babel CC0, Eco CC BY) and 8 'unverified-outside-source-jurisdiction', of which 7 are shipped plus the archival Natsume entry, which is not in dist. commercialUse is referenced nowhere in the repo's scripts or docs, so it gates nothing and is only paperwork. Marking CC0 as 'unknown' is merely over-conservative. The one reader-facing part is real: the Tagore and Natsume author pages print raw English manifest strings in the Korean credit line.
